questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is less damaging than listening to music.

questions.explanation: Long-term exposure to wind noise while riding can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Wear proper hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: A motorcycle passenger should:

options.text: Put their feet on the operator's footrests.
Wear the same protective gear as the operator.
Make the operator sit closer to the handlebars than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear the same protective gear as the operator.
questions.explanation: A passenger should wear the same protective clothing and gear as the operator. The operator should sit in their normal position when riding with a passenger.

questions.question: Which of the following is not protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Safe motorcycle riders should wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves.

questions.question: To protect a motorcycle rider, pants should:

options.text: Be made of a soft material.
Be made of a heavy material.
Fit loosely enough that they flap in the wind.
Be short and expose some parts of the legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be made of a heavy material.
questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or sturdy synthetic material that cover your entire legs. Clothing should fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind, but not so tight that it limits your movement.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Several surfaces reduce tire traction. These include wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers. Dry pavement is safer for motorcyclists than these surfaces.

questions.question: What can reduce the risk of head or neck injury in a crash?

options.text: Not allowing a passenger on the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the best way to reduce the risk of head or neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: The body eliminates one alcoholic drink per hour. If a person consumed eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks likely remain in their body?
questions.explanation: To estimate remaining alcohol, subtract the number of hours that have passed from the total number of drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining.

questions.question: When approaching an obstacle or uneven surface you cannot avoid, you should:

options.text: Make sure the motorcycle is leaning to one side.
Rise slightly off the seat to let your legs absorb the shock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slightly off the seat to let your legs absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, approach it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Slow down, keep the motorcycle upright, and rise slightly off your seat so your knees can absorb impact. Just before hitting the obstacle, roll on the throttle slightly to lighten the front end.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Have a seat that is large enough for two riders.
Only have one set of footrests.
Not encourage the passenger to wear protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn other motorists.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat that is large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have a seat large enough for two riders. It should have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear that you wear.

questions.question: A DOT-compliant helmet has all of the following, except:

options.text: Bright colors painted on the outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright colors painted on the outside.
questions.explanation: A U.S. Department of Transportation-compliant helmet must have an impact-resistant outer shell, an impact-absorbing inner liner, a comfort liner, and a chinstrap retention system. Bright colors are not required.

questions.question: Intersections are usually:

options.text: Safe because there is a lot of traffic.

questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous because many crashes happen when motorcycles and other vehicles meet there.

questions.question: For the best protection, wear a helmet certified by the:
questions.explanation: For the best protection, choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) safety standards.

questions.question: When choosing a lane position, think about:

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
How many cars are ahead of you.
Which part of the lane makes your trip shorter.
Which position lets you pass more vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should help other drivers see you. You should also keep enough space around your motorcycle to stay safe.

questions.question: ____ can remove alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: Only time reduces your blood alcohol level. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot lower your blood alcohol level or sober you up. They may keep you awake, but they don't change how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.question: What is often found in the center of a lane?
questions.explanation: Car drippings form an oily strip in the center of each lane. In dry conditions, motorcycles can usually ride safely on this center strip.

questions.question: Motorcycle riding gloves are usually:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: The body gets rid of almost ______ of alcohol per hour.
questions.explanation: Most people's bodies eliminate about one drink of alcohol per hour.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: If you can't avoid a slippery road surface, you should:

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: If you can't avoid a slippery surface, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not enough protection on its own.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should constantly look ahead for:
questions.explanation: Look ahead to stay alert. Watch for changing traffic, hazardous road conditions, and escape routes. Be ready to react quickly.

questions.question: The best way to handle someone tailgating you is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make obscene gestures.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate faster, which increases danger.

questions.question: When riding in traffic, remember that motorcycles:

options.text: Are too small to have blind spots.
Have blind spots that are too small to cause problems.
Have blind spots that require head checks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots that require head checks.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: When adjusting your rearview mirror, make sure you can see:

options.text: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
Only the lane next to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane next to you. Your mirror should show the road behind and beside you, not your helmet.

questions.question: For motorcycle safety, you should:

options.text: Assume everything on your motorcycle will work properly.
Check your motorcycle before every ride.
Check your motorcycle once a month.
Check your motorcycle twice a week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your motorcycle before every ride.
questions.explanation: Small mechanical problems are more dangerous on a motorcycle than on a car. Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride.
